3000.title: Active Arm Reach
3000.questionText: Can you raise your arm straight forward without help?
3000.patientText: Try lifting your sore arm straight up in front of you as high as you can without using your other arm to help. How far can you go?

options.label: Full overhead reach with minimal pain.
Cannot lift arm past shoulder height due to stiffness or weakness.

3100.title: Movement Comparison
3100.questionText: How does your arm move when someone else gently lifts it for you compared to when you lift it yourself?

options.label: Arm is equally stiff and painful whether you move it or someone else lifts it.
Arm moves much further or feels normal when someone else lifts it for you.
Arm is slightly limited when moved for you, but noticeably looser than when moving it alone.

3200.title: Shoulder Stiffness Pattern
3200.questionText: Is reaching behind your back or overhead severely restricted in all directions, with normal muscle strength?

options.label: Stiff and limited in all directions, but overall strength remains intact within allowed movement.
Stiffness is uneven, or accompanied by specific muscle weakness or numbness.

3300.title: Shoulder Strength Self-Test
3300.questionText: Does pressing down on your raised arm cause severe weakness or pain?
3300.patientText: Hold your sore arm out in front at a 45-degree angle with thumb pointing down. Press down lightly on wrist with other hand. What happens?

options.label: Arm drops or gives out from weakness or sharp pain.
Arm stays up and holds strong.

3310.title: Arm Hold and Position Check
3310.questionText: When you lift your arm or rotate it out, can you hold it in place or does it drift/drop on its own?
3310.patientText: Lift arm to side or rotate hand out. Try to hold it still for 5 seconds. Does arm drift backward or fall down uncontrollably?

options.label: Arm drifts or drops uncontrollably; cannot hold position.
Arm holds steady in position without dropping.

3400.title: Pinch and Arc Pain Check
3400.questionText: Do you experience pain when lifting your arm out to the side (between waist and shoulder height) or when twisting your arm inward across your chest?

options.label: Yes, severe pain during both lifting sideways and twisting inward, plus weakness pushing outward.
Pain occurs during only one of these movements (lifting sideways or twisting inward).
Neither movement causes sharp pinching or arc pain.

3500.title: Top of Shoulder Check
3500.questionText: Does pain sit directly on top of your shoulder bone, or worsen when hugging your sore arm tightly across your chest?

options.label: Yes, pain is focused on top of the shoulder bone and worsens when reaching across chest.
No pain on top of shoulder or when reaching across chest.

3510.title: Deep Joint Catching Check
3510.questionText: Do you feel deep popping, clicking, or catching inside the joint when raising your arm straight forward with thumb turned down?

options.label: Yes, deep clicking, catching, or pain inside joint during forward reach with thumb down.
No deep joint catching or thumb-down pain.

3520.title: Shoulder Slipping / Instability Check
3520.questionText: Does your shoulder feel like it wants to pop out of place when your arm is raised out to the side and rotated backward?

options.label: Yes, shoulder feels unstable, loose, or ready to slip out of socket.
No feeling of looseness or slipping.

3530.title: Joint Grinding Check
3530.questionText: Do you feel hard grinding, crunching, or a firm bony block when turning or lifting your shoulder?

options.label: Yes, noticeable hard grinding or crunching with widespread movement loss.
No hard grinding or bony block felt.

3910.title: Frozen Shoulder (Adhesive Capsulitis)
3910.primaryDiagnosis: Findings suggest frozen shoulder: equal movement restriction in active and passive tests with preserved muscle strength.

3920.title: Full-Thickness Rotator Cuff Tear
3920.primaryDiagnosis: Findings suggest significant rotator cuff tendon tear due to arm drift or inability to hold arm position against gravity.

3930.title: Partial Rotator Cuff Tear or Tendinopathy
3930.primaryDiagnosis: Findings suggest rotator cuff tendon strain or partial tear based on arc pain and weakness without arm drop.

3940.title: Subacromial Impingement
3940.primaryDiagnosis: Findings suggest tendon pinching under shoulder arch during overhead or twisting movement.

3950.title: Physical Exam Indeterminate
3950.primaryDiagnosis: Physical tests do not match a specific single classic pattern. Guided physical assessment recommended.

3960.title: Collarbone / AC Joint Strain
3960.primaryDiagnosis: Findings suggest strain or wear at joint connecting collarbone to top of shoulder blade.

3970.title: Labral / Deep Joint Tear
3970.primaryDiagnosis: Findings suggest irritation or tear in deep cartilage ring surrounding shoulder socket.

3980.title: Shoulder Instability / Looseness
3980.primaryDiagnosis: Findings suggest shoulder joint socket looseness or risk of partial slipping.

3990.title: Shoulder Joint Wear and Tear (Osteoarthritis)
3990.primaryDiagnosis: Findings suggest joint cartilage wear producing stiffness and crunching during movement.
